body:
### Problem

`vim.lsp.document_color.enable()` can hard-error with `Invalid buffer id` when it is called with a non-nil `opts`.

Two separate spots are missing a validity guard, and together they turn a stale provider into a crash:

**1. `Provider.active` can keep an entry for an already-invalid buffer.**

In `Client:_on_detach` ([`runtime/lua/vim/lsp/client.lua:1443-1459`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/client.lua#L1443)), the capability teardown loop is gated on `lsp._capability.is_enabled(Capability.name, { bufnr = bufnr, client_id = ... })`.

`is_enabled` reads `vim.b[bufnr][var]` ([`_capability.lua:248`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/_capability.lua#L248)), and reading a buffer-scoped variable on an invalid buffer **throws**:

```
:lua vim.cmd.edit('/tmp/z') local a = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() vim.cmd('bwipeout! '..a) print(pcall(function() return vim.b[a].foo end))
false   scoped variable: Invalid buffer id: 1
```

Note the line just above it, `client.lua:1435`, does guard with `api.nvim_buf_is_valid(bufnr)` before firing `LspDetach`, so `_on_detach` clearly can run with an already-invalid buffer. When it does, the loop throws before reaching `capability:destroy()`, and the provider is never removed from `Provider.active`.

**2. `Provider:clear` clears a namespace on that dead buffer, unguarded.**

`vim.lsp.document_color.enable(enable, filter, opts)` ([`document_color.lua:388-402`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/document_color.lua#L388)) sweeps **every** entry in `Provider.active` whenever `opts` is non-nil, ignoring `filter`:

```lua
if opts then
  document_color_opts = vim.tbl_extend('keep', opts, document_color_opts)
  for _, provider in pairs(Provider.active) do
    for client_id, _ in pairs(provider.client_state) do
      provider:clear(client_id)   -- <-- no nvim_buf_is_valid(provider.bufnr)
      provider:request(client_id)
    end
  end
end
```

and `Provider:clear` ([`document_color.lua:230-239`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/document_color.lua#L230)) calls `api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(self.bufnr, ...)` with no validity check.

So one stale provider poisons every later `enable(..., opts)` call, for any buffer.

Actual trace, hit while opening a Dart file after a fuzzy-finder plugin had wiped its own buffer:

```
Error executing vim.schedule callback: ...BufReadPost Autocommands for "*"..FileType Autocommands for "*"..
script .../flutter-tools.nvim/ftplugin/dart/init.lua..LspAttach Autocommands for "*":
Vim(append):Lua callback: .../lua/vim/lsp/document_color.lua:236: Invalid buffer id: 5
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'nvim_buf_clear_namespace'
        .../lua/vim/lsp/document_color.lua:236: in function 'clear'
        .../lua/vim/lsp/document_color.lua:397: in function 'enable'
        /Users/…/nvim/lua/conput/autocmd.lua:102: in function </Users/…/nvim/lua/conput/autocmd.lua:101>
        [C]: in function 'nvim_exec_autocmds'
        .../lua/vim/lsp/client.lua:1218: in function 'on_attach'
        .../lua/vim/lsp.lua:1016: in function 'buf_attach_client'
        .../lua/vim/lsp.lua:767: in function 'start'
        .../flutter-tools.nvim/lua/flutter-tools/lsp/init.lua:298: in function 'callback'
        ...
```

The user config at `autocmd.lua:101-103` is just:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('LspAttach', {
  callback = function(ev)
    vim.lsp.document_color.enable(true, { bufnr = ev.buf }, { style = '■' })
  end,
})
```

which reads as a reasonable thing to write, but passing `opts` on every attach means every attach triggers the global sweep. (Worth noting `style` is module-global state, so passing it per-buffer is redundant after the first call anyway. That's arguably a separate API wart.)

### Steps to reproduce

I could not reduce this to a clean `-u NONE` repro. Getting a stale `Provider.active` entry needs `Client:_on_detach` to run against a buffer that is *already* invalid, and the ordinary paths I tried (`:bwipeout`, `:bdelete`, `nvim_buf_delete{force=true}`, `bufhidden=wipe`) all tear the provider down correctly. In my session it took a plugin wiping a buffer out from under an attached client.

The two unguarded calls are reachable regardless of how the stale entry appears, and both are one-line fixes:

- `Provider:clear` / the `enable` sweep should skip providers whose `bufnr` is no longer valid.
- `Client:_on_detach` should either guard the capability loop with `nvim_buf_is_valid`, or `is_enabled` shouldn't throw on an invalid `bufnr`.

Happy to send a PR if the preferred shape is clear. My instinct is guarding `_on_detach` is the real fix (it stops the leak at the source) and the `Provider:clear` guard is defence in depth, but `is_enabled` throwing on a dead buffer may be the thing worth fixing instead.

### Expected behavior

`document_color.enable()` should not raise `Invalid buffer id` because some unrelated buffer was wiped earlier in the session.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1529+g06bff27929-Homebrew, LuaJIT 2.1.1788460057

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

no

### Operating system/version

macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

### Installation

Homebrew (HEAD)

The general pattern of:

"Here is an issue. Here are ways it COULD happen. Also, I cannot reproduce it."

Is not very helpful. If it is impossible to reproduce, then consider not reporting it. Or, if you think you can make safeguards to the code that'd be beneficial, also consider opening the PR yourself :)
